title: Do the thinking before you prompt
principle: The best way to get output that matches your vision is to tell Claude what you need up front. Spend time writing prompts before you design—dictate in the tool, type in Notes, or record a voice note on a walk and paste the transcript later. Figure out what you want away from the computer so Claude can execute your exact vision when you sit down.
procedure: Step away from the canvas: decide goal, audience, constraints, and success criteria before any pixels.
Capture the brief offline—voice dictation in Claude Design, phone Notes, or a walk voice-note transcript (methods Nate names).
Paste or speak the full brief before asking for visuals.
Refuse empty first prompts; iterate only after intent is written.
Revisit the brief when a remix drifts—update the written intent instead of vibes-chasing.
examplePrompts:
Before designing anything: here is the full brief I wrote offline.

Goal: <what this artifact must communicate>
Audience: <who sees it>
Constraints: <brand, format, time, fidelity>
Must include: <flows, screens, or beats>
Must avoid: <defaults or aesthetics I do not want>

Execute this vision. Do not invent a different concept.
Before any UI generation: write (1) user job, (2) refuse-list, (3) success look in 5 bullets, (4) which technique lane. Show me that plan and wait for OK.
tips: Nate: “I spend a lot of time writing prompts before I design.”
Dictation, couch Notes drafts, and walk transcripts are all valid brief-capture methods he names.
Efficiency comes from front-loading intent, not from prompting blank and hoping.

workedExamples.title: Couch / walk brief → exact vision
workedExamples.body: Nate: spend a lot of time writing prompts before designing; dictate, Notes-from-the-couch, or walk transcripts so Claude executes the vision when you sit down—not a blank-canvas improvisation. Cite: Anthropic Claude blog.

workedExamples.title: Prompt-first thrash
workedExamples.before: Jump straight into generate; thrash for an hour.
workedExamples.after: Plan gate then one ambitious prompt.
workedExamples.body: Nate: think before you prompt. Cite Anthropic blog.

workedExamples.title: Public-source honesty
workedExamples.body: Claims stay within the public Anthropic/Figma posts—no invented paywalled quotes.

antiPatterns: Opening the tool and prompting with no written intent.
Using the first empty generation as a substitute for a brief.
Skipping this step and hoping vibes carry the craft.
checklist: Fresh pass confirms the prompt constraints were followed.
promptWhy: Front-loaded brief blocks the model from inventing a different concept.
Offline thinking prevents the first token stream from locking a bad prior.

provenance.statement: Design Catalog editorial synthesis of the cited public sources; contracts and decision paths are our implementation guidance, not quotations or author endorsements.

useWhen: What can the person do after this change that they cannot do now?
avoidWhen: Do not restart discovery when the owner has already fixed the problem and direction.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Do the thinking before you prompt” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
User: [specific person]
Problem: [observable obstacle]
Outcome: [action they can complete]
Preserve: [truth, routes, constraints]
Evidence: [before/after task, not a taste score]
acceptance: Write one user/action/outcome sentence, one non-goal and a before/after example; another reader can tell whether the outcome occurred.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: A single user, action and observable outcome are named.

comparison.bad: Make the dashboard premium leaves the agent guessing what should improve.
comparison.good: Help a dispatcher find the next unassigned job names a person, an action and a result.
comparison.impact: A single user, action and observable outcome are named.
